Understanding the Transition:
"In doing so": This phrase is used to indicate that the action mentioned previously (Falconer exploring Fernández’s sculpture) leads directly to or is an example of the next idea (participating in the tradition of ekphrasis). It implies a cause-and-effect or continuation relationship between the two sentences.
When the sentence says, "In doing so, Falconer participates in a tradition...", it suggests that by exploring the sculpture in his poem, Falconer is continuing or contributing to a long-standing tradition.
